A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedFD research. All 12 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet, including accuracy, convergence, ablations, and sensitivity results in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4, Tables 1–6, and the experimental figures.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged, including hierarchical feature alignment, orthogonal projection, feature distillation loss, and the training and aggregation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three image-classification datasets and retain the same heterogeneity, scalability, and CNN/ResNet scenarios. Neither reports LLM experiments.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain HeteroFL, MOON-hetero, FedFusion-hetero, FedGen-hetero, DaFKD-hetero, FedMD, MSFKD, and FedGD. Comparator membership also matches in the remaining tables and learning-curve comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported protocols are identical, including data partitioning, accuracy metrics, model configurations, 10 local epochs, 200 communication rounds, 20 clients, and a 0.4 participation ratio.

E4.justification: The logit-distillation analysis, component ablations in Table 3, model-heterogeneity analysis in Table 4, scalability tests in Table 5, and architecture comparison in Table 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify two runs per experiment and calculate averages and variability using each run's final ten rounds. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the experimental figures retain identical numerical entries, curves, and findings. No results are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their accompanying assumptions and derivations are unchanged, including feature aggregation, matrix-exponential orthogonality, and the KL objective.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same core claims about FedFD's feature alignment, orthogonal projection, modularity, privacy and communication properties, and superior accuracy.

C2.justification: V2 deletes the Limitations paragraph following Section 5. V1 explicitly acknowledged untested LLM applicability and discussed client hardware constraints and small-client/large-server knowledge-transfer challenges. This discussion is not relocated; other interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, model construction, and data-processing information are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: V2 removes 'enhancing performance and privacy' from the introductory description of reference [36] and deletes the limitations paragraph's LLM research-gap statement. The cited works and dedicated Related Work section remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The author block expands from one author to seven with revised affiliations and contacts. A short introductory clause and the final limitations paragraph are deleted; the remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author block alters first-page spacing and pushes one introductory line onto page 2. Removing Limitations leaves additional white space on page 9. Figures, tables, and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 retains the scientific content but removes v1's explicit acknowledgement of untested LLM applicability and associated deployment and transfer barriers. This modestly reduces transparency about applicability. The authorship and brief editorial changes provide no clear compensating improvement in scientific explanation or evidence.
